what: A fine noise grain covers the background (three.js shader) — the panel is split into 120 × 120 cells, each cell mixes two hash noises, the coverage .25 edge is cut with a smooth step (smoothstep), and only where noise exists is the background color pulled toward the grain color (green-gray) by strength .25 × opacity .25. Opacity · coverage are multiplied by the square root of the pixel ratio. Every 120 seconds the grain drifts one step, very slowly within .1 cell, so it looks like paper grain without flicker

options.freq · size: Number of cells (one side of the grid), default 120 · cell size multiplier 1 (cells ÷ size)

note: three loads three.cjs after three-global.js as a regular <script> Loaded as such. The background color is read once when attached to the panel (the panel’s background color, or --kf-bg if none). The original drew with EffectComposer’s ShaderPass over an empty scene, which gives the same result as a single full-panel shader, so it is drawn that way

from.where: shared.js full-screen noise texture (original NoisesScene — three r173, size 1 · frequency 120 · opacity .25 · coverage .25 · tintColor #9CA18C · tintStrength .25 · speed 120 · speedJitter .1, screen-fixed canvas z-index 100)
